newsitem.title: USA: USDA pleased with pact with Mexican tomato growers.
newsitem.headline: USDA pleased with pact with Mexican tomato growers.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department Secretary Dan Glickman Friday said he was pleased an agreement had been reached with Mexican tomato growers.

"This agreement demonstrates that U.S. trade laws can be effective in protecting U.S. industries from unfair competition without unduly restricting trade and adversely impacting consumers," Glickman said in a statement.

The Commerce Department announced earlier it had reached a tenative agreement with Mexican growers to settle a bitter trade dispute. Under the proposed settlement, Mexican tomato growers would agree to not sell their produce in the U.S. at less than a certain price, called the reference price.

The proposed agreement will settle a controversial complaint brought by Florida tomato growers against Mexican producers for allegedly selling their produce in the United States at below market prices and costing the U.S. industry hundreds of millions of dollars in lost sales.
